wordings.SITU_STEPS_SENTENCE: A gate projection and an up projection read the same array. The gate branch is bounded by 4 tanh(x / 4) and multiplied by its own sigmoid, the up branch is bounded by 25 tanh(x / 25), the two branches are multiplied, and a down projection maps the product back.
wordings.SITU_BOUND_SENTENCE: A bounded tangent is close to the identity for a value much smaller than its bound and never leaves the interval between minus the bound and the bound, so SiTU behaves as a SwiGLU on small values and caps the large ones.
DENSE_MLP_DESCRIPTION: The feed-forward map of layer 0, one SiTU-GLU of width 33,792 computed once per token.
Layers 1 to 92 hold a mixture of experts in its place.
wordings.GATE_DESCRIPTION: The router of one token. A linear map scores all 896 experts in FP32, and a sigmoid maps each score into the interval from zero to one. A learned correction bias is added to one copy of the scores, and the 16 experts with the highest biased scores are kept. The other copy, which holds no bias, is read at the kept experts, so the bias decides which experts run and does not scale their outputs. The 16 gates are divided by their sum plus the epsilon of the router. The configuration sets the route scale to 1, so the gates of a token sum to one.
ROUTED_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: The 16 experts kept by the router, each a SiTU-GLU of width 3072 that reads and writes the latent of 3584 channels with its own weights.
Each weight produces the expert axis, so its implicit weight holds all 896 experts, and the diagonalisation after the down projection keeps the entries where the slot and the expert agree.
wordings.LATENT_DESCRIPTION: The routed experts of one token run on a latent of 3584 channels, half the hidden width. The hidden state is projected onto the latent, the 16 kept experts read it, one contraction over the 16 slots multiplies each output by its gate and sums the products, the sum is normalised by an RMS normalisation over the latent, and a second projection maps it back onto the hidden width. A server that places the experts on many processors sends the latent to the processor holding an expert, which moves half the bytes the hidden state would.
SHARED_EXPERT_DESCRIPTION: The two shared experts, written by the reference as one SiTU-GLU of width 6144, which is twice the width of a routed expert. Every token runs them on the hidden state.
wordings.MIXTURE_DESCRIPTION: The mixture of experts of one token, which stands in layers 1 to 92. The router keeps 16 of the 896 experts and gives each a gate, the kept experts run on the latent, and the output of the shared experts is added. The mixture is computed once per token.
wordings.QUERY_PATH_DESCRIPTION: The queries of the latent attention. The hidden state is projected onto a low rank of 1536 channels and normalised by an RMS normalisation, and one projection gives each of the 96 heads a query of 192 channels. The reference cuts the 192 channels into 128 and 64 and joins them again in the same order, so the query is one projection.
wordings.KEYS_AND_VALUES_DESCRIPTION: The keys and the values of every head of the latent attention. The hidden state is projected onto a latent of 512 channels per token and normalised. One projection of the latent gives 128 channels of the key of each of the 96 heads, and a second gives the 128 channels of the value of each head. A separate projection of the hidden state gives 64 channels per token, which are copied to every head and joined after the 128 channels of the key. No channel is turned by a rotary embedding, because the configuration sets mla_use_nope. The reference computes the projection of the hidden state as one weight, kv_a_proj_with_mqa, and the projection of the latent as one weight, kv_b_proj, and cuts each result with torch.split.
wordings.CORE_DESCRIPTION: The softmax of one query of one head over the tokens at or before it. The query scores against the key of every such token, and every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the head width of 192. A softmax over the tokens turns the scores into weights that are positive and sum to one, and the weights sum the values. A distance that counts back past the first token holds no value, and the softmax and the sum pass over it. The core is computed once per query and head.
wordings.OUTPUT_GATE_DESCRIPTION: The gate of the latent attention. A projection of the hidden state gives one number for every channel of every head, and a sigmoid maps each into the interval from zero to one. The output of every head is multiplied by the gate before the output projection, because the configuration sets mla_use_output_gate.
wordings.MLA_DESCRIPTION: The attention of 24 of the 93 layers, multi-head latent attention as in DeepSeek-V3 with no rotary embedding and with a sigmoid gate on the output of every head. The keys and the values of every head are expanded from a latent of 512 channels per token, and the keys and the values are read back from each query at every token at or before it. The core of every query and head, the gate and the output projection follow. The reference caches the keys and the values of every head.
wordings.CONVOLUTION_DESCRIPTION: A causal convolution of four taps over every channel of every head, followed by the SiLU. Tap i_w of token i_x reads the channel of token i_x - i_w, and every channel has four weights of its own, which is what makes the convolution depthwise. A tap before the first token holds no value, as the padding of three zeros in front of the sequence does in the reference. The reference stores the weights of a channel from the oldest token to the newest, and the tap axis counts back from the newest, so tap i_w holds the weight stored at 3 - i_w.
wordings.L2_NORM_DESCRIPTION: Divides one head of one token by its length over the 128 key channels, after adding the epsilon of the kernel to the sum of the squares. The query and the key then have length one, so the product of a query and a key lies between minus one and one whatever the size of the projections. The reference passes use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel, and chunk_kda applies the normalisation before the recurrence.
wordings.DELTA_QKV_DESCRIPTION: The queries, the keys and the values of the delta attention. Three projections of the hidden state give each of the 96 heads 128 channels. Each projection passes through its own causal convolution of four taps and a SiLU. The queries and the keys are divided by their length over the 128 channels, and the queries are multiplied by one over the square root of 128, which is the default scale of chunk_kda.
wordings.DECAY_DESCRIPTION: The decay of every key channel of every head. The hidden state is projected onto a rank of 128 and back onto the 12,288 channels of the heads. The bias of the channel is added, the sum is multiplied by the exponential of a learned number of the head, and the gate of fla writes the logarithm of the decay as -5 times the sigmoid of the product. The decay therefore lies between the exponential of -5, about 0.0067, and one. The reference passes the raw projection to chunk_kda, and the kernel computes the gate before the recurrence.
wordings.STRENGTH_DESCRIPTION: The strength of the write of every head, a projection of the hidden state onto one number per head passed through a sigmoid. The strength scales how far the delta rule moves the state towards the value at the key. The reference passes use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel, and chunk_kda applies the sigmoid before the recurrence.
wordings.SCAN_STEP_DESCRIPTION: One token of the delta rule, repeated once per token. The iteration reads its token of the queries, the keys, the values, the decays and the strengths, grabs the state of every head and the output so far, and drops the next state and the next output for the next iteration. Every row of the state is multiplied by the decay of its key channel. The key reads the value the decayed state predicts, the difference between the value and the prediction is multiplied by the strength and by the key, and the product is added to the state. The query reads the new state, and the result is written at the position of the token.
wordings.SCAN_DESCRIPTION: The gated delta rule over the tokens. Every head holds a state of 128 key channels by 128 value channels, which starts at zero and is carried from each token to the next. The reference computes the recurrence with chunk_kda of fla, in blocks of 64 tokens, and naive_recurrent_kda of the same package states it one token at a time. A server that decodes one token at a time keeps the state of every head in place of the keys and the values of every earlier token, so the memory of a delta layer does not grow with the context.
wordings.DELTA_OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION: The output of the scan normalised by an RMS normalisation over the 128 value channels of each head, with a gain shared by the 96 heads, and multiplied by the sigmoid of a projection of the hidden state onto every channel of every head. The reference computes the two steps in one kernel, FusedRMSNormGated with the sigmoid activation. An output projection maps the result back onto the hidden width.
wordings.KDA_DESCRIPTION: The linear attention of 69 of the 93 layers. The queries, the keys and the values are projected and convolved over the last four tokens, and the queries and the keys are normalised. The decay of every key channel and the strength of every head are read off the hidden state. The scan carries a state of 128 by 128 numbers per head from each token to the next, and the output of every token is normalised, gated and projected back onto the hidden width. The layer holds no cache of keys and values.
wordings.MIX_DESCRIPTION: The input of a sublayer read off the entries of the attention residuals of one token. Entry 0 holds the embedding, entry 1 + i holds the sum of the outputs of block i of twelve layers, and the entry of the current block holds the sum of its outputs so far. Every entry is normalised by an RMS normalisation and scored by a learned vector, a softmax over the entries turns the scores into weights, and the weights sum the entries. An entry after the current block holds no value, and the softmax and the sum pass over it. Every sublayer holds its own gain and vector, so each chooses how much of each earlier block it reads.
wordings.RESIDUAL_DESCRIPTION: One sublayer and the attention residuals around it. The sublayer reads a mix of the entries, normalised by an RMS normalisation with a learned gain, and its output is added to the entry of the current block. Every layer holds two such sublayers, the attention first and the feed-forward map second.
wordings.FIRST_LAYER_DESCRIPTION: Layer 0 runs the delta attention and the dense MLP. Its attention reads the embedding directly, because the reference applies no mix while the list of finished blocks is empty. The mix before the dense MLP reads the embedding and the output of the attention.
wordings.DELTA_LAYERS_DESCRIPTION: Layers that run the delta attention and the mixture of experts, one after another.
wordings.LATENT_LAYER_DESCRIPTION: A layer that runs the gated latent attention and the mixture of experts.
wordings.GROUP_TITLE: \text{Three Delta Layers and a Latent Layer}
wordings.GROUP_DESCRIPTION: Four layers of the plan, three with the delta attention and one with the latent attention, which is the ratio of three to one the configuration sets by listing the layers. Every group adds its outputs to the entry of the block it stands in.
wordings.FIRST_BLOCK_DESCRIPTION: The first block of twelve layers, whose outputs are summed at entry 1 of the attention residuals. Layer 0 holds the dense MLP, layers 1 and 2 the delta attention, layer 3 the latent attention, and layers 4 to 11 two groups of three delta layers and a latent layer.
wordings.REPEATED_BLOCKS_DESCRIPTION: Six blocks of twelve layers, each three groups of three delta layers and a latent layer. Block o + 1, for the counter o from 0 to 5, sums its outputs at entry o + 2, so the sum of every earlier block stays at an entry of its own.
wordings.LAST_BLOCK_DESCRIPTION: The last block, of nine layers, whose outputs are summed at entry 8. Two groups of three delta layers and a latent layer are followed by layer 92, a second latent layer in a row, because the configuration lists both 92 and 93 among the latent layers and counts from one.
wordings.EMBEDDING_BLOCK_DESCRIPTION: The token identifiers are looked up in a table of 163,840 rows of 7,168 channels, and the lookup gives one hidden state per token. The hidden state is written at entry 0 of the attention residuals, and every later entry starts empty. The vision encoder writes image features into the embeddings of an image placeholder, and a prompt of text passes the embeddings to the layers unchanged.
wordings.OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION: A last mix of the attention residuals reads the embedding and the sums of the eight blocks. The mix is normalised by an RMS normalisation and projected onto the 163,840 entries of the vocabulary, which gives the logits of the next token. The configuration sets tie_word_embeddings to false, so the output head has weights of its own.
wordings.TOP_K_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: Keeps the 16 largest biased scores and hands them out on the sparse expert axis k/e, whose extent is the 896 experts and which has 16 live positions. The live positions record which experts were kept.
wordings.SELECT_DESCRIPTION: Reads the unbiased scores at the experts kept by the selection and multiplies each score by the value held there by the selection, which is one after the indicator. The result rides the sparse expert axis of the selection.
wordings.EMBEDDING_DESCRIPTION: Looks up the row of the embedding table named by the token identifier. The table holds one row of the hidden width for every entry of the vocabulary.
wordings.KEY_JOIN_DESCRIPTION: Joins the 128 key channels expanded from the latent and the 64 key channels shared by the heads into the 192 channels of a key. The shared channels come after the expanded ones, as in the torch.cat of the reference.
wordings.WRITE_AT_ENTRY_DESCRIPTION: Writes an array at one entry of the attention residuals and leaves every other entry empty. The addition after it puts the array into the entry, because an empty entry added to a value gives the value.
wordings.WRITE_AT_TOKEN_DESCRIPTION: Writes the output of one token of the scan at the position of that token and leaves every other position empty. The addition after it puts the output into the array of outputs.
wordings.BACK_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Counts tokens back from each query. Distance i_r of query i_x reads token i_x - i_r. A distance that counts back past the first token holds no value, and the guarded axis r|x records which distances hold no value. The reference passes is_causal to the attention kernel, which states the same restriction.
wordings.REPEAT_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Copies the 64 shared key channels of a token to every head. The reference writes the copy as an expand, which allocates no memory.
wordings.DIAGONAL_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Keeps the entries where the slot and the expert agree. The down projection produces an output for every expert at every slot, and each slot reads the output of its own expert.
wordings.TAPS_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Counts tokens back from each token over the four taps of the convolution. Tap i_w of token i_x reads token i_x - i_w. A tap before the first token holds no value, and the guarded axis w|x records which taps hold no value.
wordings.DEPTHWISE_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Keeps the entries where the channel of the filter and the channel of the value agree. The taps produce a filter for every channel at every channel, and each channel reads its own filter, which is what makes the convolution depthwise.
wordings.EMBEDDING_ENTRY_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Reads entry 0 of the attention residuals, which holds the embedding. The attention of layer 0 reads it directly.
wordings.TOKEN_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Reads the position of the current token, the counter i_x of the loop, so that each iteration of the scan reads the queries, the keys, the values, the decays and the strengths of its own token.
wordings.QUERY_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the query low rank of 1536 channels. The reference names the weight q_a_proj.
wordings.QUERY_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the normalised low rank onto the 192 channels of the query of every head. The reference names the weight q_b_proj.
wordings.LATENT_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the key-value latent of 512 channels. The weight holds the first 512 rows of kv_a_proj_with_mqa.
wordings.SHARED_KEY_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the 64 key channels every head shares. The weight holds the last 64 rows of kv_a_proj_with_mqa.
wordings.KEY_EXPANSION_ROLE: Expands the normalised latent into the 128 key channels of every head. The weight holds the rows of kv_b_proj that give the keys.
wordings.VALUE_EXPANSION_ROLE: Expands the normalised latent into the 128 value channels of every head. The weight holds the rows of kv_b_proj that give the values.
wordings.LATENT_OUTPUT_GATE_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the gate of every channel of every head of the latent attention. The reference names the weight g_proj.
wordings.LATENT_OUTPUT_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the gated output of the 96 heads of the latent attention back onto the hidden width. The reference names the weight o_proj.
wordings.DELTA_QUERY_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the 128 query channels of every head of the delta attention. The reference names the weight q_proj.
wordings.DELTA_KEY_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the 128 key channels of every head of the delta attention. The reference names the weight k_proj.
wordings.DELTA_VALUE_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the 128 value channels of every head of the delta attention. The reference names the weight v_proj.
wordings.QUERY_TAPS_ROLE: The four taps of the convolution of the queries, one filter for each of the 12,288 channels. The reference names the module q_conv1d.
wordings.KEY_TAPS_ROLE: The four taps of the convolution of the keys, one filter for each of the 12,288 channels. The reference names the module k_conv1d.
wordings.VALUE_TAPS_ROLE: The four taps of the convolution of the values, one filter for each of the 12,288 channels. The reference names the module v_conv1d.
wordings.DECAY_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the rank of 128 the decays are read through. The reference names the weight f_a_proj.
wordings.DECAY_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the rank of 128 onto every key channel of every head. The reference names the weight f_b_proj.
wordings.DECAY_BIAS_ROLE: One learned number per key channel of every head, added to the projection before the gate. The reference names the array dt_bias and keeps it in FP32.
wordings.DECAY_RATE_ROLE: One learned number per head, whose exponential multiplies the biased projection before the gate. The reference names the array A_log and keeps it in FP32.
wordings.STRENGTH_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto one number per head, the strength of the write before its sigmoid. The reference names the weight b_proj.
wordings.DELTA_OUTPUT_GATE_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the gate of every channel of every head of the delta attention. The reference names the weight g_proj.
wordings.DELTA_OUTPUT_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the gated output of the 96 heads of the delta attention back onto the hidden width. The reference names the weight o_proj.
wordings.ROUTER_ROLE: Scores every one of the 896 experts from the hidden state of a token. The reference computes the scores in FP32.
wordings.CORRECTION_BIAS_ROLE: One learned number per expert, added to the scores before the choice of the 16 experts and to no gate. The reference names the array e_score_correction_bias.
wordings.LATENT_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the latent of 3584 channels the routed experts read. The reference names the weight routed_expert_down_proj.
wordings.LATENT_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the normalised sum of the routed experts from the latent back onto the hidden width. The reference names the weight routed_expert_up_proj.
wordings.EXPERT_GATE_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the latent onto the gate branch of every routed expert. The reference names the weight w1 of each expert.
wordings.EXPERT_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the latent onto the up branch of every routed expert. The reference names the weight w3 of each expert.
wordings.EXPERT_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the product of the two branches of every routed expert back onto the latent. The reference names the weight w2 of each expert.
wordings.SHARED_GATE_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the gate branch of the shared experts. The reference names the weight gate_proj.
wordings.SHARED_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the up branch of the shared experts. The reference names the weight up_proj.
wordings.SHARED_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the product of the two branches of the shared experts back onto the hidden width. The reference names the weight down_proj.
wordings.DENSE_GATE_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the gate branch of the dense MLP of layer 0. The reference names the weight gate_proj.
wordings.DENSE_UP_PROJECTION_ROLE: Projects the hidden state onto the up branch of the dense MLP of layer 0. The reference names the weight up_proj.
wordings.DENSE_DOWN_PROJECTION_ROLE: Maps the product of the two branches of the dense MLP back onto the hidden width. The reference names the weight down_proj.
wordings.ATTENTION_MIX_WEIGHT_ROLE: Scores every normalised entry of the attention residuals before the attention of a layer. The reference names the weight self_attention_res_proj, and the gain of the normalisation is self_attention_res_norm.
wordings.FEED_FORWARD_MIX_WEIGHT_ROLE: Scores every normalised entry of the attention residuals before the feed-forward map of a layer. The reference names the weight mlp_res_proj, and the gain of the normalisation is mlp_res_norm.
wordings.OUTPUT_MIX_WEIGHT_ROLE: Scores every normalised entry of the attention residuals before the output head. The reference names the weight output_attn_res_proj, and the gain of the normalisation is output_attn_res_norm.
wordings.OUTPUT_HEAD_ROLE: Maps the final hidden state onto the logit of every entry of the vocabulary. The reference names the weight lm_head.
wordings.EMBEDDING_TABLE_ROLE: The table of 163,840 rows of 7,168 channels, one row per entry of the vocabulary. The reference names the table embed_tokens.
wordings.ATTENTION_SCALE_ROLE: Multiplies every score of the latent attention by one over the square root of the head width of 192, so the spread of the scores does not grow with the width.
wordings.QUERY_SCALE_ROLE: Multiplies every normalised query of the delta attention by one over the square root of the 128 key channels, which is the scale chunk_kda takes when it is given none.
wordings.SIGMOID_ROLE: Maps every value into the interval from zero to one. The router scores, the write strengths and the two output gates pass through it.
wordings.SILU_ROLE: Applies the SiLU after each causal convolution, which multiplies each value by its own sigmoid.
wordings.INDICATOR_ROLE: Replaces every kept biased score by one, so the selection keeps its positions and forgets its values.
wordings.SITU_GATE_ROLE: Bounds the gate branch of a SiTU-GLU by 4 tanh(x / 4) and multiplies it by its own sigmoid. The reference computes it in FP32 inside SituAndMul.
wordings.SITU_UP_ROLE: Bounds the up branch of a SiTU-GLU by 25 tanh(x / 25). The reference computes it in FP32 inside SituAndMul.
wordings.DECAY_ROLE: Turns the scaled projection into the decay of a key channel. The logarithm of the decay is -5 times the sigmoid of the value, so the decay lies between the exponential of -5 and one.
wordings.EXPONENTIAL_ROLE: Turns the learned number A_log of a head into the factor that scales the projection before the gate.
wordings.INVERSE_LENGTH_ROLE: Turns the sum of the squares of a head into one over its length, with the epsilon of the kernel added to the sum.
wordings.NEGATE_ROLE: Negates the value predicted by the decayed state, so the addition after it gives the difference between the value and the prediction.
